edges.explanation: Both articles identify the same structural logic: when a measurable input (consumption hours; macroeconomic conditions) becomes abundant or weakens, it decouples from the outcome that actually drives value (revenue per unit of attention; company-level performance), forcing decision-makers to optimize for the scarce complement (quality of focus/intent; internal operational resilience) rather than the surface metric.

Both articles expose how organizations systematically optimize for easily measurable metrics (consumption hours, board composition credentials) while remaining blind to the actual quality drivers that determine outcomes (focus + intent for monetization, structural independence + skeptical judgment for governance), revealing a common structural failure where quantifiable surface measures mask the qualitative conditions that genuinely produce value.

Both articles identify the same structural logic: when supply becomes near-infinite (25,000x more YouTube hours than TV; one-third of global trade growth concentrated in AI semiconductors), per-unit economics of the abundant resource collapse while quality of the scarce complement (focused attention; geopolitically aligned partnerships) becomes the true value driver that surface metrics obscure.

Both articles identify a specific structural failure where surface-level confidence metrics (board composition credentials in Article B; company-level optimism in Article A) mask underlying governance and decision-making vulnerabilities—the same logic that confidence in *who* or *what* you're confident about diverges from capacity to *recognize* actual risks.

Both articles reveal the same structural logic: actors insulated from macro shocks through strategic positioning (business leaders via company-level resilience, trade partners via geopolitical realignment and AI-sector growth) can thrive locally even as aggregate systems deteriorate, suggesting that fragmentation into aligned sub-networks creates pockets of immunity to systemic stress.
